cards.name: Lens mode toggle with tap or hold
cards.summary: The camera-weapon view opens on a firm fresh button press, turns the view toward the nearest visible ghost, and closes on a second tap or on release after a longer hold.
cards.behavior: Pressing the lens button enters aim mode only if the pad reports at least a light-pressure threshold, so a feather touch is ignored, and the press must be a fresh one. Entry is refused while the player is paralyzed or confused, or while a locked animation runs. On entry the reticle jumps to screen center, the shutter lock is armed, and the nearest living, visible ghost inside a fixed radius becomes a heading target. The look pitch snaps to that ghost at once, while the body yaw is covered by a constant step each update over a 25-update transition, after which the mode flips to full aim. The shutter lock only counts down once full aim has started, so it runs after that transition. To leave, the player either taps the button again (toggle) or releases it after having held it longer than a tap threshold (hold-to-aim); a lowering animation then plays before normal control returns.

cards.name: Reticle drift and look rates in aim mode
cards.summary: Stick input slides a small reticle inside a tight box while the view yaws and pitches at three selectable rates.
cards.behavior: Each update the stick, or the d-pad at a fixed offset, is read, and an axis only counts once it passes a deflection gate. With input, the reticle moves up to a couple of pixels per update in the stick direction and is clamped to a small rectangle around screen center; with no input it glides back to center at a slightly slower step. View yaw and pitch change by a coarse step when the stick is pushed far or the d-pad is used, by a very fine step for a small deflection, and by a double-size step while a speed button is held. Pitch is clamped to sixty degrees each way, and the eye sits at a head offset above the feet (a lower one in one special stance), looking one thousand units along the aim vector. A zoom lens upgrade lets two shoulder buttons change the field of view by a small step per update inside a fixed range.

cards.name: Viewfinder frame and focus-circle test
cards.summary: A ghost counts as framed when it sits inside a fixed pixel rectangle, in range, inside the view cone and unobstructed; a smaller circle and a bullseye add bonuses.
cards.behavior: Every living ghost is projected to screen space each update. It must lie within a fixed distance of the player, inside a forward cone around the player heading, and inside a rectangle centered on the reticle. Being framed raises one flag; being within a focus circle around the reticle raises a second flag and stores the distance; being within a tiny radius of the reticle raises a bullseye flag. A ghost also needs a clear view: a point nudged toward the camera must pass a depth test, unless the player is very close. A ghost is then a valid capture target when it is in the focus circle, or very near and framed, while it is visible and not fully faded. The circle radius grows with a lens upgrade, and a captured ghost is what makes the charge meter rise.

constants.name: Frame height
constants.unit: screen pixels, tested against the vertical coordinate doubled

cards.name: Charge meter that rises while a ghost is framed
cards.summary: Holding a ghost in capture fills a charge counter, faster when it is close; emptying the frame drains the meter one level at a time.
cards.behavior: While a valid ghost is captured, a degree counter grows each update by a rate that is a base factor plus a proximity bonus, times a fixed multiplier; the bonus scales from nothing at two thousand units to the full amount at point-blank. When the counter passes a threshold set by the speed upgrade, the level goes up by one and the counter resets, with one sound for a level-up and another for reaching the cap. The cap depends on the lens upgrade, and the weakest film type is capped at one level. At the cap the displayed rate is pinned to a fixed value. The meter drains only when no ghost at all is inside the frame; a ghost that is framed but outside the focus circle or hidden behind something holds the meter where it is. While draining, the counter counts down from its current partial value (restarting from a cooldown set by the speed upgrade only if it is zero or above that cooldown), and the level drops by one whenever it hits zero, until the film base level is reached; better film starts higher.

constants.unit: unitless, added to the base factor at point-blank

cards.name: Shutter, film spending and photo freeze
cards.summary: The shutter fires on a fresh press, burns one film, resets the charge and freezes the player, camera and ghosts while the result plays.
cards.behavior: The shutter ignores presses during the entry lock, needs a fresh press, and is blocked while the player is paralyzed or a photo is still being processed. It needs at least one film of the selected type unless an infinite-film setting is on; with none, a dry-click sound plays instead. On a valid shot the damage for each captured ghost is computed, the score data is gathered, any quick-turn is cancelled, the shutter sound is picked from the charge band, and the charge resets to the film base level. The shot sets a freeze timer that holds player control, the camera and ghost updates; the result stage later overwrites that timer with a short value for a kill, a very short one for a non-kill during a fight, and a longer one for an ordinary shot. A second timer records a recent shot so ghost scripts can react to being photographed.

cards.name: Charge-indexed damage ladder
cards.summary: A shot reads its damage from a 22-entry ladder indexed by charge level plus bonuses for a chance window, a bullseye and better film.
cards.behavior: The index starts at the current charge level. It adds three when the ghost is in a chance state, two when the reticle is within the bullseye radius, and a fixed bonus for the film type, then clamps at the top entry. The chance state is a window a ghost opens while it winds up a lunge: a script raises a flag, and the engine promotes it when the player is within the ghost chance range during its attack. The ladder runs from ten damage in steps of ten up to two hundred and ten, with a final entry of two hundred and fifty. The ghost takes that value as pending damage, and the shot is marked as a killing shot when its health is no greater than the damage. A chance-window hit also sets a knockback flag and tags the hit with a heavier type when the meter is full.

cards.name: Shot score from distance, centering and bonuses
cards.summary: Score is a point total built from charge and proximity bonuses, times a ratio made of distance, centering, charge and kill factors.
cards.behavior: Points start at the charge level, add one for being inside the ghost reach range, one for near-perfect centering, two for a full meter and four for a chance-window hit, then multiply by twenty-five for the main ghost class or twelve for the lesser class. Overkill adds a fraction of the excess damage. A separate ratio multiplies a distance factor (high inside the reach range, falling to half over about two thousand units beyond it), a centering factor (highest within a tiny circle, falling to half at a hundred pixels), a charge factor for a full meter, a chance factor, and a kill factor: a non-kill is scaled down, a killing shot is scaled up, and a killing shot that also has both a full meter and a chance-window hit is scaled up further. A ghost that is faint gets half the ratio and a solid one gets a little extra. The final score is never below the shot damage, because points are forced up to the damage when the product would be lower.

cards.name: Four lens abilities that stagger, slow, freeze or reveal
cards.summary: Spending a special charge item applies one of four timed effects to every ghost currently inside the lens.
cards.behavior: Each ability fires on a button press and spends one special item. It affects only ghosts that are alive, inside the lens, not in an immune state and not already under another lens effect. The push ability forces the ghost into a stagger action; the slow ability sets a long timer during which the ghost moves at half its normal step; the freeze ability sets a shorter timer and halts the ghost fully; the reveal ability sets a long timer and raises the ghost to a fixed visibility. If no ghost qualified, a miss sound plays instead of the ability sound. Damage cancels all of these timers.

cards.name: Ghost wander, notice, chase and attack states
cards.summary: Each ghost cycles between wandering, notice, pursuit and attack according to damage, proximity, facing, footsteps and line of sight.
cards.behavior: A ghost re-evaluates awareness each update while in its wander, notice or pursuit action, though a countdown can delay this. Ghosts that lack the reactive attribute simply pursue. A reactive ghost that has not noticed the player moves to notice when it was just hurt, when the player is inside its gather distance, inside that distance and within its front half-plane, or making noise: running footsteps carry farther than walking ones. It ignores the player when the player is not in one of its assigned rooms. Once alerted, it becomes pursuit when a sampled line to the player is clear of walls, doors and furniture, and falls back to notice when something blocks it. In pursuit, a ghost starts an attack when the player is within its attack range and the line is clear; in attack, it gives up and returns to wandering when the player is farther than the attack range plus a margin.

cards.name: Data-driven ghost behavior scripts
cards.summary: A ghost has no hard-coded behavior; each state looks up a byte-coded script and a small interpreter runs one command at a time with waits.
cards.behavior: When a ghost enters a state, three nested offset tables (by ghost class, ghost id, then state number) point at that state script and the interpreter is rearmed with a one-update wait. Each update the wait counter counts down; when it reaches zero the next byte selects a command handler from a table of one hundred and sixteen handlers, and handlers chain in a loop until one sets a nonzero wait. Commands cover setting position, setting walk or run speed from the ghost data, turning toward the player, picking a patrol point, blinking next to the player, striking, attacking, playing sounds, jumping inside the script and ending the state. A special wait value ends the script until a new state is chosen. The interpreter is skipped while a time-stop flag is set, and ghosts also run a second small script for visibility blinking.

cards.name: Waypoint travel toward the player
cards.summary: A ghost heads for the route node that is both reachable and nearest the player, turning slowly toward it while walking or running.
cards.behavior: The command scans a small route table for nodes at the same height with a clear sampled line to the ghost, and keeps the two nearest. Of those two it picks the one nearer the player, so the ghost drifts toward the player along the graph. If none qualifies it drops the height and clear-line checks and retries; if the table is empty it snaps the ghost onto the player position. The ghost speed comes from its data, walk or run depending on a script parameter, and the heading turns a few degrees per update toward the node. Arrival is tested on the axis the ghost is mostly facing, so it stops once it has passed the node along that axis.

constants.name: Heading turn rate
constants.unit: degrees per update at 60 Hz NTSC

cards.name: Blink teleport near the player
cards.summary: A ghost jumps to a script-chosen distance and bearing from the player and stays invisible there for a short time before appearing.
cards.behavior: The command picks a distance from two script bytes, in units of fifty world units, then picks a bearing: directly behind the player, a random ten-degree step around the full circle, or straight ahead. It converts that offset to a world position around the player, moves the ghost there at once, keeps its height, refreshes its position data and plays a sound. Only then, if a hide time is given, does it set the ghost visibility to zero at the new spot, wait that many updates, and restore the saved visibility, so the ghost fades in already standing at its ambush point.

cards.name: Strike reach test, swipe versus grab
cards.summary: A ghost lunges only when the player is inside reach, roughly in front and at similar height; the result is either a quick hit or a held grab.
cards.behavior: The reach test compares distance to a reach value from the ghost data: a shorter one while the player is looking through the lens, a longer one otherwise, and it requires a small vertical gap and a narrow facing cone. On success the script jumps to the attack branch. The attack command forces a quick hit instead of a grab when a percent roll passes, or when the player is in a door animation, already damaged or at a different height. A grab holds the player for the ghost attack time multiplied by thirty updates, sets a short forced injured walk afterward, and places the ghost in front of the player; a hit applies damage and a stagger. On hard difficulty the base damage is multiplied by two and a half.

cards.name: Damage, stagger and death reaction
cards.summary: A hit lowers ghost health; during a chance window it staggers, otherwise it flashes, and lethal damage selects a death state.
cards.behavior: Pending damage is consumed once per update, and consuming it clears all lens effect timers. A ghost flagged as immune ignores damage unless the hit landed in a chance window. If damage meets or exceeds health, health goes to zero and the death action is queued. Otherwise health drops by the damage; a hit in a chance window queues the stagger action, and any other hit requests a hit flash. The hit also sets a flag that wakes the awareness logic, so a damaged ghost always notices the player. A flash request runs a short sequence: a sound, a forced visibility value, then a wait of one hundred and twenty updates before the flags clear. These reactions outrank the normal rules, as does the retreat action used when the player leaves the ghost area.

constants.name: Flash sequence wait
constants.unit: updates at 60 Hz NTSC (one game update per vsync; 50 Hz on PAL)

cards.name: Queued health drain and revival item
cards.summary: Damage is a pending amount that drains two health per update, and a spent revival item refills health instead of ending the run.
cards.behavior: A hit sets the pending-damage amount (overwriting any remainder rather than adding to it); while that amount is nonzero the player loses two health each update until it is empty. A new hit during the drain is ignored unless it carries priority, and hits are ignored for the whole refill after a revival. When health reaches zero the game checks for a revival item: if one is held, it is spent, the drain stops and health refills five per update up to the maximum. Otherwise the game-over sequence starts, or a mission-failed screen in the battle mode. At or below a low-health threshold a heartbeat loop plays, and below a similar threshold the idle pose changes to a hurt stance.

cards.name: Dodge window against a grab and struggle
cards.summary: When a ghost grabs, the player has an 18-update window to dodge with exactly one press; failing that, flicking the stick shortens the hold.
cards.behavior: A grab does not damage at once. For an 18-update window the game counts presses: any dodge input in the first eight updates is flagged as too early, while presses after that count one each, and throwing the stick to full tilt counts as a clean dodge. Only exactly one late press with no early press avoids the grab, so mashing the button fails. On a clean dodge the damage is skipped and the ghost attack timer is cleared; otherwise the damage is queued and the player stays held. While held, each new full-tilt stick direction that differs from the last one shortens the remaining grab timer by three as long as more than twenty-two updates remain, and the pad rumbles. The hold ends when the timer reaches zero, and a recovery animation plays.

cards.name: Controller pulse that speeds up near ghosts
cards.summary: A pulsing rumble and heartbeat sound warn of the nearest ghost: closer ghosts give shorter gaps and stronger pulses.
cards.behavior: Every update the nearest living ghost that is not mid-attack is found. Inside a fixed range, the distance in five-hundred-unit bands indexes two tables: one for the gap between pulses and one for pulse strength, so the closer the ghost the shorter the gap and the stronger the pulse. A pulse plays a heartbeat sound at its start and lasts a fixed number of updates; the gap timer only counts down between pulses, and self-roaming ghosts give half strength. With no ghost nearby, a rare apparition or a hint object within a shorter range gives a slower, weaker pulse on a long fixed gap.

cards.name: Locomotion speed and gradual turning
cards.summary: Movement speed mostly comes from animation root motion, with fixed fallback speeds for blends; turning is gradual with a rapid pivot for large angle changes.
cards.behavior: Each update the player speed is set from the current animation: the root-motion distance of the frame, scaled by a fixed factor, and a fixed table of fallback speeds only while animations are blending. The table has one value each for running, walking, aiming strafe and injured walking, plus small values for stairs and ladders. The stick angle is rebased by the angle from the room camera to the player, so up on the stick always means away from the camera. The heading turns toward that angle in fixed steps while moving; when the difference is large it starts a rapid pivot at a higher rate for as many updates as needed. Walk or run is chosen by a run button, and a forced injured walk overrides both. The game runs one update per vsync, so the per-update values here hold at 60 Hz NTSC; the PAL build multiplies movement by 1.2 to compensate for 50 Hz.

cards.name: Input continuity across a camera cut
cards.summary: When a fixed room camera cuts, the player keeps the old world heading so the stick does not suddenly point somewhere new.
cards.behavior: When the active camera number changes while the player is moving, a short hold starts during which the player keeps moving along its current heading and the stick is not re-mapped. When the hold ends, the game compares the bearing from the player to the old camera position with the bearing to the new camera. If the view changed by more than a fixed angle, the current stick angle is remembered and the old mapping stays in force until the stick is released or moves away from the remembered angle by more than a smaller tolerance. In the common case of a small cut the new mapping takes effect after the hold. This keeps fixed-camera movement smooth through cuts.

cards.name: Fixed room cameras and kind switching
cards.summary: Each room zone has authored camera records chosen by zone, with separate kinds for exploring, fights, cutscenes and doors.
cards.behavior: Each update the game picks one of four camera kinds: ordinary room cameras, a battle set while a fight is active, a drama set that cutscenes request, and a door set while a door sequence runs. Within a kind, the current zone number selects a record whose type decides how the camera is placed: a fully fixed pose, a fixed position that looks at the player, or a position that slides along a segment as the player moves through the zone, with roll and field of view interpolated along the same fraction. A change of camera records the previous camera position for the movement mapping. While a ghost damages the player, a close-up camera glides toward a point near the player at a fixed speed.

cards.name: Door interaction, lock state and the open sequence
cards.summary: A door opens when the player presses the action button inside its trigger area facing it; the player is parked on the door mark while the next room loads.
cards.behavior: The action button turns on a one-update check that tests whether the player stands in a door trigger polygon on the front or back side, whether the door is unlocked, and whether the player heading is inside the door allowed angle range. If so, the player is frozen and the next room starts loading. The player is placed on the door mark and aligned with the door heading (the start and end poses are equal, so there is no glide), and the player animation is requested with a 40-update blend. The open-wait counter only starts once the room load finishes; after a short count the door slot is registered as opening and its sound plays, and the end of the player animation moves the player to the far side. Locks are a separate flag from the state enum; locking or unlocking forces the state back to closed. There are twenty door slots in a room.

cards.name: Event triggers and the event command interpreter
cards.summary: Story events open on authored conditions and run through a byte-coded script that marks each command done as it goes.
cards.behavior: Each room offers sixteen candidate event slots. An event opens when it has not yet run, all of its required event flags are set, all required items are held, and its trigger kind is satisfied: automatic, action button pressed, item used, photo of a given subject, or end of a battle. Most kinds are blocked during a fight. A position check requires the player to face the event point inside a cone and range; one kind alternatively passes when the player is very close. While running, the interpreter walks the event bytes every update; each command carries a done byte, so finished commands are skipped, and blocking ones such as messages or movies end the pass until they finish. Command lengths are a few bytes, and the done flag is written into the script data itself.
